newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, nearbys weak.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, nearbys weak.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed mixed, with nearby March and May weak on evidence of increased wheat moving from the country, traders said.

"If there's any feature, it's not that we're seeing hedging tied to new sales but rather that railcars are finally making their way to the elevators for loading, meaning that the backlog of existing sales is finally easing and the pipeline is filling up," a MGE trader said.
USDA's Market News Service said 359 cars and 10 trains of spring wheat were received on the Minneapolis cash trading floor Thursday. Basis levels were broadly lower.

MGE spring wheat closed 1-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 1/4 cent higher, with March down 1-3/4 cents at $3.87-1/2. Traders said the March/May spread traded between 17 and 18 cents throughout the session.
Volumes were light, and traders said Benson-Quinn and Continental each sold at least 500,000 May bushels.
MGE barley did not trade and closed unchanged, with March at $6.50 per cwt.
